To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have successfully expressed and purified the GCGR-Ecd and the GCGR-EcD-Gc fusion protein in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic expression systems and determined their in vitro binding affinity to glucagon.
the expression and purification of recombinant GCGR-ECD were achieved and the binding affinities between glucagon and GCGR-Ecd were determined.
we have successfully expressed, purified, and characterized the extracellular domain of glucagon receptor (Gcgr), a class B G-proteins coupled receptor (GPCR) that is the receptor of glucagon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the successful production of both prokaryotic and eukaryotic GCGR-ECD for further structural studies.
the expression, purification, and preliminary characterization of GCGR-ECD, a promising candidate for the structure determination of GCGR.
the expression of GCGR-ECD, which is the first step for the structural determination of GCGR and the development of its antagonist.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression and purification methods reported in this paper are useful for the production of GCGR-ECD for structural study.
the expression, purification and initial characterization of GCGR-ECD has been achieved.
the prokaryotically expressed GCGR-Ecd can serve as a functional receptor for glucagon in vitro, and the fusion protein GCER-Ecd-Gc is a good candidate for structural study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prokaryotically expressed GCGR-E CD is a good candidate for future structural studies of the GCGR.
we developed a robust expression and purification system for GCGR-ECD, and obtained high quality GCGR-ECD for future structural studies.
the expression and purification method developed in this study would be applicable to the production of other GPCR extracellular domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GCGR-Ecd can be expressed and purified in a relatively high yield, which will be used in future studies for the structural characterization of GCGR.
the MBP fusion and the DsbC coexpression approach are useful tools for the expression of the GCGR-EC and its fusion protein in the prokaryote.
the GCGR-E CD can be expressed as a soluble protein in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic systems.
